## Purpose

Follow-up to #47896 (TurboQuant FlyDSL decode) and #57057 (UltraQuant FlyDSL
decode), addressing review feedback that both kernels lean on low-level FlyDSL
APIs that are unstable or slated for deprecation. The kernels are rewritten
against FlyDSL's public `fx.*` API, following aiter's
`flydsl-kernel-code-cleanup` guide.

It also fixes a load failure on the pinned stack (`AITER_BRANCH=v0.1.24.post1`,
flydsl 0.3.4.1): neither FlyDSL decode kernel currently loads on main, and both
silently fall back to Triton. `tq_decode.py` / `tq_decode_gqa6.py` import
`buffer_ops` and `vector` from `flydsl.expr`, and `ultraquant_decode_hd256.py`
imports them from aiter internals (`aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels`); none of these
exist in the pinned versions. After this PR the kernels use only public FlyDSL
APIs and no aiter internals.

No behaviour change: outputs are bit-identical to the merged kernels on every
tested shape.

## Changes

| Legacy API | Replacement | UQ | TQ |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ArithValue` / `arith.*` / `_mlir.ir` types | typed `fx.Int32` / `fx.Float32` / `fx.Vector`, Python operators | done | done |
| raw `scf.ForOp` / `scf.IfOp` | `range(..., init=[...])`, Python `if` / `const_expr` | done | done |
| `buffer_ops.*` | `fx.rocdl.make_buffer_tensor` views + `fx.copy` with `BufferCopy` atoms (`buffer_utils.py`) | done | done |
| raw `rocdl.mfma_*` / `mfma_scale_*` | `fx.make_mma_atom` + `fx.gemm` (`mma_utils.py`) | done | done |
| `s_waitcnt(0xC07F)` | `rocdl.s_waitcnt(lgkmcnt=0)` | done | done |
| `SmemAllocator` / `SmemPtr` | `fx.SharedAllocator` | done | DONE |
| stale / verbose comments, dead code | trimmed (AST-checked) | done | done |

## Test Results

| Check | UltraQuant | TurboQuant |
|---|---|---|
| Outputs vs merged kernels | 15/15 bit-exact | 11/11 bit-exact |
| ISA vs merged kernels | 15/15 identical | 9/11 identical; 2 TGPP>1 cases rescheduled |
| Kernel tests | 64 passed (both files) | |
| Serve smoke, auto backend | Qwen3.6-27B (GQA-6): pass | Qwen3-32B (GQA-8): pass |
| Serve smoke, explicit backend | Qwen3.6-27B: pass | Qwen3-32B: pass; MiniMax-M2.5 TP=2 (GQA-6): pass |

GPQA-Diamond, Qwen3.8-27B, `ultraquant_4bit`, TP=2, seed 7:

| Run | Correct / 198 |
|---|---|
| Merged UQ PR, earlier runs | 177, 179, 179, 180 |
| This PR | 177 (89.4%), 0 errors, 0 truncated |

GPQA-Diamond, Qwen3.6-27B, `ultraquant_4bit`, TP=2 (correct / 198). The
merged-kernel row reruns the #57057 kernel on today's stack, same seed and
settings:

| Run | seed 42 | seed 123 | seed 7 | mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Merged UQ PR (as reported) | 171 | 173 | 172 | 86.9% |
| Merged UQ kernel, today's stack | | 171 | | |
| This PR | 169 | 168 | 172 | 85.7% |

Earlier reruns of the merged PR at seed 7 ranged 169–173; the kernels are
bit-exact, so the spread is run-to-run batching nondeterminism.

GSM8K, Qwen3-32B, `turboquant_4bit_nc`, TP=1, 1319 samples, 5-shot (same
lm-eval command as the #47896 validation runs):

| Run | strict-match | flexible-extract |
|---|---|---|
| #47896 FlyDSL TQ, Jul 30 | 73.84 | 63.31 |
| #47896 BF16 KV, Jul 30 | 74.75 | 62.55 |
| This PR | 73.84 | 63.91 |

| Run | Output tok/s | Req/s | ITL avg / p50 (ms) | TTFT p50 (ms) | Requests (errors) |

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

block_base = phys_block * _stride_cache_block is i32, and every K/V/meta load goes through the single kv_buf4/kv_buf_i16 view on the cache base (L203-204). Once a layer's TQ cache view reaches 4 GiB, the voffset wraps. Because num_records is 0xFFFFFFFF, it silently reads another block instead of faulting. The merged kernel has the same issue, but main never runs it on the pinned stack (it falls back to int64 Triton), and this PR turns it back on. UQ already folds a 64-bit block base into the descriptor (ultraquant_decode_hd256.py:449-455). Small eligible models on one MI355X get past 4 GiB: about 5.3 GB/layer for Qwen2.5-3B and about 6.5 GB/layer for Qwen2.5-1.5B (GQA-6). Could you mirror UQ (fx.Int64(fx.Uint32(phys_block)) * stride passed as base_byte_offset), or at least gate FlyDSL on the cache view being under 4 GiB, and add a >4 GiB TQ case?

nodes.body: Q is always bitcast to bf16 here, but the launcher pools q_rot with dtype=q_dtype (flydsl_turboquant_decode.py:272). The TQ backend allows fp16, and the eligibility check doesn't look at dtype. An fp16 model (e.g. Qwen3-32B-AWQ) with turboquant_4bit_nc therefore gets silently wrong attention: the fp16 and bf16 builds produce byte-identical ISA. The bug predates this PR, but this PR makes it reachable. Fix: allocate the pooled q_rot as torch.bfloat16, or gate eligibility on bf16.

detail.body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #47896 (TurboQuant FlyDSL decode) and #57057 (UltraQuant FlyDSL
decode), addressing review feedback that both kernels lean on low-level FlyDSL
APIs that are unstable or slated for deprecation. The kernels are rewritten
against FlyDSL's public `fx.*` API, following aiter's
`flydsl-kernel-code-cleanup` guide.

It also fixes a load failure on the pinned stack (`AITER_BRANCH=v0.1.24.post1`,
flydsl 0.3.4.1): neither FlyDSL decode kernel currently loads on main, and both
silently fall back to Triton. `tq_decode.py` / `tq_decode_gqa6.py` import
`buffer_ops` and `vector` from `flydsl.expr`, and `ultraquant_decode_hd256.py`
imports them from aiter internals (`aiter.ops.flydsl.kernels`); none of these
exist in the pinned versions. After this PR the kernels use only public FlyDSL
APIs and no aiter internals.

No behaviour change: outputs are bit-identical to the merged kernels on every
tested shape.

## Changes

| Legacy API | Replacement | UQ | TQ |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ArithValue` / `arith.*` / `_mlir.ir` types | typed `fx.Int32` / `fx.Float32` / `fx.Vector`, Python operators | done | done |
| raw `scf.ForOp` / `scf.IfOp` | `range(..., init=[...])`, Python `if` / `const_expr` | done | done |
| `buffer_ops.*` | `fx.rocdl.make_buffer_tensor` views + `fx.copy` with `BufferCopy` atoms (`buffer_utils.py`) | done | done |
| raw `rocdl.mfma_*` / `mfma_scale_*` | `fx.make_mma_atom` + `fx.gemm` (`mma_utils.py`) | done | done |
| `s_waitcnt(0xC07F)` | `rocdl.s_waitcnt(lgkmcnt=0)` | done | done |
| `SmemAllocator` / `SmemPtr` | `fx.SharedAllocator` | done | DONE |
| stale / verbose comments, dead code | trimmed (AST-checked) | done | done |

## Test Results

| Check | UltraQuant | TurboQuant |
|---|---|---|
| Outputs vs merged kernels | 15/15 bit-exact | 11/11 bit-exact |
| ISA vs merged kernels | 15/15 identical | 9/11 identical; 2 TGPP>1 cases rescheduled |
| Kernel tests | 64 passed (both files) | |
| Serve smoke, auto backend | Qwen3.6-27B (GQA-6): pass | Qwen3-32B (GQA-8): pass |
| Serve smoke, explicit backend | Qwen3.6-27B: pass | Qwen3-32B: pass; MiniMax-M2.5 TP=2 (GQA-6): pass |

merged-kernel row reruns the #57057 kernel on today's stack, same seed and
settings:

| Merged UQ PR (as reported) | 171 | 173 | 172 | 86.9% |
| Merged UQ kernel, today's stack | | 171 | | |
| This PR | 169 | 168 | 172 | 85.7% |

Earlier reruns of the merged PR at seed 7 ranged 169–173; the kernels are
bit-exact, so the spread is run-to-run batching nondeterminism.

GSM8K, Qwen3-32B, `turboquant_4bit_nc`, TP=1, 1319 samples, 5-shot (same

+"""Buffer-resource (V#) views shared by the FlyDSL decode kernels.
+
+The descriptor sits in SGPRs and each access adds a 32-bit voffset, so offsets
+into one view must stay below 4 GiB; move the base with ``base_byte_offset``
+for anything further away.
+"""
+
+import flydsl.expr as fx
+
+# Nominal view extent. The real bound is the descriptor's num_records, which
+# make_buffer_tensor() leaves at 0xFFFFFFFF bytes (no OOB checking).
+_VIEW_ELEMS = 0xFFFFFFFF
+
+
+def buffer_view(tensor, elem, unit_elems=1, base_byte_offset=None):
+    """Buffer view of a kernel tensor argument, indexed in ``elem`` elements.
+
+    ``view[i]`` loads or stores one element. With ``unit_elems > 1``,
+    :func:`load_vec` / :func:`store_vec` access ``unit_elems`` consecutive
+    elements starting at any element index ``i``.
+    """
+    it = fx.get_iter(tensor)
+    if base_byte_offset is not None:
+        it = fx.add_offset(fx.recast_iter(fx.Uint8, it), base_byte_offset)
+    elem_ptr = fx.PointerType.get(elem.ir_type, fx.AddressSpace.Global, elem.width // 8)
+    it = fx.recast_iter(elem_ptr, it)
+    if unit_elems == 1:
+        layout = fx.make_layout(_VIEW_ELEMS, 1)
+    else:
+        layout = fx.make_layout((_VIEW_ELEMS, unit_elems), (1, 1))
+    return fx.rocdl.make_buffer_tensor(fx.make_view(it, layout))
+
+
+def _copy_atom(elem, n, cache_modifier=0):
+    return fx.make_copy_atom(fx.rocdl.BufferCopy(n * elem.width, cache_modifier), elem)
+
+
+def load_vec(view, index, n, cache_modifier=0):
+    """Load ``n`` elements at element ``index`` of a ``unit_elems=n`` view."""
+    elem = view.element_type
+    frag = fx.make_rmem_tensor(n, elem)
+    fx.copy(_copy_atom(elem, n, cache_modifier), fx.slice(view, (index, None)), frag)
+    return fx.Vector(frag.load())
+
+
+def store_vec(view, index, value, n):
+    """Store the ``n``-element vector ``value`` at element ``index``."""
+    elem = view.element_type
+    frag = fx.make_rmem_tensor(n, elem)
+    frag.store(value)
+    fx.copy(_copy_atom(elem, n), frag, fx.slice(view, (index, None)))
